answer: A reef of trusted agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each newcomer to stake a refundable deposit and complete a slow, verifiable history of useful work before gaining full rights. Like a nebula condensing into stars, reputation should accumulate gradually, not appear overnight. Attackers who spawn thousands of fake identities then face a steep delta: every clone costs real capital locked for weeks plus compute spent on tasks, while honest agents reuse one earned identity. Sybil farms become unprofitable when cloning costs exceed any reward from gaming the system.
